title: The Columbian Exchange
text: The Columbian Exchange refers to the widespread transfer of plants, animals, culture, human populations, technology, diseases, and ideas between the Americas and the Old World (Afro-Eurasia) following Christopher Columbus's 1492 voyage. The Americas contributed foods such as maize, potatoes, tomatoes, chocolate, vanilla, and tobacco to the rest of the world, dramatically changing diets globally. Europe and Asia sent horses, cattle, pigs, wheat, and rice to the Americas. The most devastating aspect of the exchange was the introduction of Old World diseases — smallpox, measles, influenza — to populations with no prior exposure. Epidemics killed an estimated 50–90% of indigenous American populations within decades.
